title: Traffic shielding experiment runner for gradual model upgrades
creator: Anika Bose
description: Ship an experiment runner that performs progressive traffic ramps (shadow -> canary -> A/B cohorts) for model version upgrades with built-in statistical stop checks, exposure limits, and automated rollback triggers. The runner should integrate with the routing layer, Redwood Console rollout UI, and Redwood Optimize signals so PMs and SREs can safely run experiments without manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Enable configuration of staged exposure schedules (percentages, durations, and hold windows) per experiment
Run automatic statistical tests (preconfigured metrics: latency, token-error rate, regression on eval set, output-quality score) at end of each hold window and decide continue/hold/rollback
Support shadow mode that mirrors production traffic to candidate model without impacting responses
Expose experiment status and decision rationale in Console timeline and API
Auto-rollback performed when configurable thresholds breached and rollback documented in audit log
Integrates with routing policy so traffic is routed to fallback models during partial outages
milestones: Proto: shadow + single-step canary with manual approve (2025-02-07)
Add statistical tests and automatic decisioning (2025-02-21)
Beta with internal teams, observe and iterate (2025-03-10)
notes: We want to minimize surface area on the router: implement experiment runner as a control-plane orchestration that updates routing rules rather than in-path inference proxies.
Statistical tests will use sequential analysis with early stopping to limit exposure time for sharp regressions.
Default metric set will be opinionated but configurable per-experiment; allow customers to supply custom metric hooks via Console or webhook.
Trade-off: more aggressive auto-rollback reduces risk but increases churn for ephemeral model upgrades—expose guardrails as PM-configurable profiles (conservative / balanced / aggressive).
risks: False positives from noisy metrics may cause unnecessary rollbacks; mitigation: require multiple metrics or repeat failure across hold windows before rollback
Coordination with Dedicated/private control planes may add latency to rollout steps; mitigation: design a fallback polling mechanism
Complexity of exposing decision rationale could leak internal eval data; mitigation: redact sensitive fields in UI and logs
